question: Name the French jeweller who travelled to India at least six times during the Mughal period.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jean-Baptiste Tavernier.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Jean-Baptiste Tavernier** was a **French jeweler and traveler** during the Mughal period.
 
• Tavernier made **at least six trips** to India between **1630 and 1668,** during which he collected **precious stones and gems **for his business in Europe.
 
• Tavernier was known for his keen eye for **spotting valuable gems **and his ability to **negotiate with local merchants** and rulers in India.
 
• Tavernier's** travels and writings** about India provided valuable insights into the **Mughal court and society**, as well as the trade networks that connected India with the rest of the world.

 
• **Antonio Monserrate** was a **Portuguese Jesuit missionary** and traveler in India during the 16th century.

 
 
• While he was **not a jeweler, **he did write extensively about the **Mughal court and society. **
 
 
 
• **Seydi Ali Reis** was a **Ottoman admiral and traveler **in the 16th century.
 
 
• He did **not **travel to India during the Mughal period.
 
 
 
• **Peter Mundy **was an **English merchant and traveler** in India during the 17th century.
 
 
• He did **not** have a background in jewelry or gemstones.
